analysis.title: US Color, China Industrial Tech 2027 Outlook
key_insights: S&P 500 closed -4.36% at 7,353, its worst day since 4/4/25. NDX fell 6.36%, its worst day since March 9, 2020. SOX fell 12%, its worst day since 2020.

The selloff centered on semiconductors and AI adjacencies as the market recalibrates datacenter gigawatt build forecasts and the execution path after this week's election news. The weakest groups were E&C (datacenter construction), IPP/power, neoclouds and semiconductors.
SOX multiples have compressed about 50% from the June/July highs. The desk says the next investor debate is whether downside risks to GW and capex outlooks have been overpriced.
NASDAQ VIX had its biggest 1-day move since Covid and is back near Liberation Day levels. VVIX rose nearly 45 points, the 2nd largest 1-day rise ever behind Volmageddon.

High Beta Momentum fell 6.2% and is 51% off its June highs, the worst drawdown in more than 10 years. ETFs were 32% of tape volume, the largest share since June. Many GS AI baskets had their biggest down day since the launch of ChatGPT.
Futures closed below the medium-term CTA threshold of 7,549. The desk expects incremental US supply, with the down 2.5 stdev estimate from this morning at -$7.48bn in S&P for sale over the next week.

GS flows: the franchise has net sold -$27bn of Tech (Info Tech + Comm Services) since this Tech unwind began, more than the -$21bn in the July technical unwind. Today's net sell was -$3bn, of which Tech was -$2.2bn. Info Tech has been net sold for 6 straight sessions and 4 of the past 5 weeks.

Hedge fund performance: Global Fundamental LS -1.3% (a -2 SD move, YTD +8.7%). TMT funds fell more than 4% and are roughly flat to slightly positive YTD, versus about +24% before the June/July AI sell-off. US-focused funds -1.7% (YTD +5.5%). Systematic LS +0.2%. Multi-Strats -1.4%, with Momentum down 3.7 SD.

GS credit (Amanda Lynam): hyperscaler YTD global debt issuance is $296bn, above GS's full-year 2026 forecast of $250bn. That is 36% of GIR's 2026 capex forecast, versus GS's initial 33% expectation. Some of it is pull-forward of 2027 supply.

GS credit sees risks to its forecasts tilted toward more spread widening between now and early December. It still assumes 35% of hyperscaler 2027 capex is debt financed, roughly $440bn of direct issuance.

GS China Industrial Tech 2027 Outlook favors the AI robotics supply chain and Data Center Electricals. Overseas data center progress is solid, though 800VDC mass adoption is delayed to 2028. GS forecasts China grid investment +6% y/y in 2027, with more emphasis on UHV.

GS cuts 2026-2030 China industrial tech sector EPS estimates by 5-10% on average, mainly in battery and energy storage names, on raw-material inflation and margin pressure. It upgrades Jianghai (002484.SZ) to Buy with a 12m TP of Rmb43.9.

Nintendo: 2Q operating profit of ¥73.9bn missed expectations on weak Switch 2 hardware sell-in despite a software beat. GS keeps Buy and a ¥9,800 TP, cuts FY27E operating profit 6% to ¥401.8bn and FY28E-FY31E by 2-7%.

Sony: 2Q operating profit of ¥622.3bn beat on record box office for Spider-Man: Brand New Day and PlayStation engagement. Management raised FY3/27 operating profit guidance to ¥1,870bn. GS raises FY3/27-FY3/31 operating profit estimates 6-9% (¥160/USD assumption) and raises its TP to ¥4,800 (Buy).
Other rating changes listed: Kuehne & Nagel down to Neutral, Australia gold miners (GMD down to Neutral, RRL to Sell, NEM/RMS/CMM more defensive), Saudi Tadawul Group upgraded to Buy.

Most-read items include Americas Utilities early views on state election results, with potential risk to TX-exposed power stocks including NRG and VST. Another is a GS note that Democrats won a House and Senate majority with gains well above expectations.

tension_points.bull_case: The desk says the debate may shift to whether downside risks to GW and capex outlooks have been overpriced, after SOX multiples compressed about 50% from the June/July highs.
